title: Still waiting to see Winona Ryder onstage someday! 🤞
transcript: Ranking the eight Stranger Things actors that I have seen do live theater I did a version of this before but I'm updating to include Joe Keery sadly in last place is my beloved Sean Aston seeing him as Santa Claus in Elf the musical was very cute and charming but no great feat of stage acting. in seventh place David Harbour as Achilles in Troilus and Cressida in 2016 and he actually only did about nine performances of this before, I kid you not, he injured his Achilles tendon and had to drop out. And he was solid, he fit the role but it was not a very memorable performance. and next I do have Joe Keery currently on Broadway in other Desert Cities playing kind of a jaded cool guy caught in the middle of this family drama. it's totally in his wheelhouse he has a few moments where he really shines but he kind of fades into the background for a lot of the show. next I have Alex Breaux who, fun fact is in Stranger Things on screen as the Lieutenant but also in the Broadway show. I've actually seen him in many plays over the years though including actually in that same production of Troilus and Cressida. and he's a real pro always a really strong charismatic presence. in fourth place Gabriela Pizzolo who plays Dustin's girlfriend in Stranger Things and she was in Fun Home at the second time I saw it and she was great maybe not like the next level brilliant performance that Sidney Lucas gave but still super talented. in third place I have Maya Hawke who I actually thought was perfectly cast in Sarah Ruhl’s Eurydice last year she was a perfect match for the sort of tender quirky charm of the writing and in fact I thought she was better in this than in Stranger Things in a close second place I have Gaten Matarazzo who I've seen on stage three times: he was the best part of Sweeney Todd he was excellent in Parade and I actually saw him as Gavroche in Les Mis too and you know I remember! like sometimes with child actors you don't realize that you saw them until like flipping through the Playbills years later but no he was a very memorable Gavroche. but in first place you might think I'm giving it to Sadie Sink because of John Proctor is the villain and yes partly absolutely but it's mostly because I saw her play Annie in 2013 and to this day she is still the best performance I've seen in that role she completely broke my heart and is partly why I fell in love with that musical
